title: STILL PRESENT (r3): wrong-person awaiting UPDATE still executes unguarded — the taken_over_at backstop SQL exists but the handler never calls it, and the race pin is vacuous
evidence: form_handler.gleam:1250: `sql.update_reference_call_status(config.db, id_uuid, sql.AwaitingCorrection, "", "contact_invalid", sql.ContactInitiated,)`; update_reference_call_status.sql: `WHERE id = $1 AND status = $5::reference_call_status` (no taken_over_at clause); mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person.sql: `AND taken_over_at IS NULL` — its only caller is sql.gleam:1891 definition + the test; test:1746: `rc_sql.mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person(db, call)` (direct SQL call, never the POST route)
detail: Round-4 mandate both conditions fail: (1) the executed wrong-person transition is still the unguarded update_reference_call_status — a take-over between the token read and the UPDATE still yanks a landlord-handled row (status unchanged by take-over) into awaiting_correction; (2) the race test calls the guarded SQL directly while the handler uses a different UPDATE — vacuous pin.
recommended_fix: Call mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person in apply_wrong_person's awaiting branch (0-row = stand down); rewrite wrong_person_awaiting_sql_has_taken_over_backstop_test to POST the wrong-person route with a take-over between read and UPDATE, and neutralize the backstop to prove it bites.
